answer: Paced arrival gating. Each new identity must spread its first N requests as a decaying ripple over a fixed window, with inter-arrival gaps matching a per-identity schedule. Bursts above the cap are throttled, not rejected, so automation gains nothing. Enforced at the ingress lagoon, this ties throughput to elapsed time rather than resources: an attacker pays in wall-clock delay per identity, and parallel sybils each burn their own umber waiting period, making mass creation linearly expensive in time.
